key_insight: The paper turns normally harmful hyperfine intermediate states into a resource to both preserve adiabaticity and speed up a CNOT gate in an EIT-based Rydberg-atom protocol.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to faster, high-fidelity quantum gates that better fit within coherence-time limits in atomic quantum hardware.
method: Use EIT-based adiabatic CNOT control with hyperfine intermediate states in two-photon transitions.
Optimize pulses so HISs enhance the STAY pathway and accelerate population transfer in the TRANSFER pathway.
Extend the model to include decay from multiple HISs and arbitrary numbers of states.
evidence_signal: In realistic Cs atomic setups, the optimized protocol achieves gate fidelities above 0.9991 in 0.3903 microseconds.
watch_item: Performance may be sensitive to decay in intermediate states and to how well the optimized pulses and atomic parameters can be realized experimentally.
paper_title: Fast Adiabatic Quantum Gates via Hyperfine Intermediate States
